//: Lighthouse CI — desktop. Budgets guard the five metrics we care about:
FCP, LCP, Speed Index, TBT and CLS.
Budgets are calibrated against what a GitHub runner actually measures,
not a developer laptop. Recorded medians for whoever retunes them:
/   FCP  444  LCP  444  SI  444  TBT 0  CLS 0.006  (laptop)
TBT is deliberately the loosest budget here, and that is a property of the
runner rather than of the site. Measured on a GitHub ubuntu-latest two-core
box, three consecutive runs of the same commit gave 299, 657 and 325 ms —
against 2 ms on a developer laptop. Lighthouse applies a 4x CPU throttle on
top of a machine already sharing cores with other tenants, so TBT tracks who
else is on the hardware. Playwright's CI guidance makes the same point about
browser work needing the whole machine to be reproducible. The budget is set
above the worst observed run so it catches a real main-thread regression
rather than a busy afternoon; tightening it means moving to a larger runner.
Paint metrics do NOT have this problem — FCP, LCP and Speed Index came back
within ~20% of laptop values on the same runner, so those budgets are tight.
CLS stays absolute at 0.1 — the Core Web Vitals 'good' boundary — because
both sites sit near zero and a relative budget there would track drift.
Runs against the built static output, so the check is deterministic and
needs no deploy. CDN headers and edge latency are Netlify's checks.
